hints: Simplify the first term to $7\sin\theta$ and replace $\cos^2\theta$ with $1 - \sin^2\theta$.
Rearrange all terms onto one side into standard quadratic form $a\sin^2\theta + b\sin\theta + c = 0$.
walkthrough:
Expand the left-hand side of $\cos\theta(7\tan\theta - 5\cos\theta) = 1$ using $\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$:
$$\cos\theta\left( 7\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} - 5\cos\theta \right) = 7\sin\theta - 5\cos^2\theta = 1$$

Rearrange into quadratic form with integer coefficients:
$$5\sin^2\theta + 7\sin\theta - 6 = 0$$

hints: Use the quadratic from part (a) with argument $2x$: $5\sin^2(2x) + 7\sin(2x) - 6 = 0$.
Find all angles for $2x$ in the interval $0^\circ < 2x < 360^\circ$ and divide each by 2.
walkthrough:
Apply the identity from part (a) with $\theta = 2x$:
$$5\sin^2(2x) + 7\sin(2x) - 6 = 0$$

Solve $\sin(2x) = 0.6$ for $0^\circ < 2x < 360^\circ$ (given $0^\circ < x < 180^\circ$):
$$\text{Principal angle: } 2x = \arcsin(0.6) \approx 36.87^\circ \implies x = \frac{36.87^\circ}{2} \approx 18.4^\circ$$
$$\text{Second quadrant: } 2x = 180^\circ - 36.87^\circ = 143.13^\circ \implies x = \frac{143.13^\circ}{2} \approx 71.6^\circ$$
